files.purpose: Owns the in-app self-update install pipeline and the observable progress model that drives the About page's version pill slider: milestone fractions, download to a temp .dmg, hdiutil mount plus ditto copy-out, codesign/version/Gatekeeper verification, and a /bin/sh installer script that swaps the bundle after the app quits and relaunches it.

File writes: downloads to FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>.dmg

Writes <staging>/install.sh (UTF-8, atomically) and creates an empty <staging>/install.log used as stdout+stderr for the installer process

Process launches: /usr/bin/hdiutil attach (timeout 120), /usr/bin/ditto (timeout 300), /usr/bin/hdiutil detach -force (timeout 60), /usr/sbin/spctl --assess (timeout 120), and /bin/sh <install.sh> <pid> <staged> <destination>
Deletes the downloaded .dmg after the copy (try? removeItem) on both the success and the error path
UserDefaults write/remove of "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion"
Quits the app: NSApp.terminate(nil) 350 ms after handoff
Shows a modal NSAlert on failure
Timers: 125 ms creep tick task, 600 ms failure-reset task, 25 s handoff timeout task, 350 ms pre-terminate delay
Haptics feedback on begin, on failure, and once per milestone crossed
The installer script itself removes the staging tree, moves the installed bundle to a hidden .<name>.previous backup, runs xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine and open on the destination
platform_assumptions: macOS AppKit: NSAlert, NSApp.terminate, @MainActor UI isolation
Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) and structured concurrency Task/Task.sleep
Apple Security framework code-signing APIs (SecStaticCode, SecRequirement) and the codesign requirement language

Apple certificate OIDs in the requirement: anchor apple generic, certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] (Developer ID CA), certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] (Developer ID Application)
Gatekeeper via /usr/sbin/spctl --assess --type execute
Apple disk images: /usr/bin/hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly -noautoopen -mountpoint, and detach -force
/usr/bin/ditto for bundle-preserving copy; xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine; open(1) to relaunch
App-bundle layout: the update is a .app directory found by pathExtension == "app" at the image root, and the running app is Bundle.main.bundleURL inside a writable parent folder (Applications)
POSIX shell /bin/sh with kill -0 polling, trap '' HUP, and POSIX file permissions 0o700
persisted_fields: "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion" (UserDefaults.standard, String) — the version the handoff promised; set just after the installer process starts, removed if the handoff times out after 25 s, and consumed once on the next launch by consumeRelaunchMarker(), which returns true only when it equals AppInfo.version
ui_elements: Failure alert: messageText "Update Failed", informativeText = error.localizedDescription, alertStyle .warning, shown with runModal()
Progress slider milestone fractions the version pill renders: 0.05 preparing ceiling, 0.55 download end, 0.70 verify end, 0.82 staging ceiling, 0.86 handoff end, 0.96 install dot, 1.0 complete
Creep rates: preparing 0.05 toward 0.05; unknown-size download 0.012 toward 0.50; verifying 0.12 toward verifyEnd - 0.02 (0.68); staging 0.10 toward 0.82
Creep tick every 125 ms, advancing by remaining * rate and stopping when remaining <= 0.0005
Failure shows .failed for 600 ms then resets to idle (fraction 0)
Celebration mounts at 0.86 and sweeps to 1 with firesHaptics: false
feature_notes: install() is a no-op when an install is already running or when AppInfo.isDevelopment is true

Install sequence reported to the progress model: begin() -> download with byte fractions -> beginVerification() -> stage() -> beginStaging() -> handOff() -> noteHandoff(); any throw calls fail() and shows the alert
The track only moves forward: apply() clamps to 0...1 and returns early unless the new value is strictly greater than the current fraction
Haptics fire once per milestone crossed: .levelChange at handoffEnd (0.86), .alignment at the other dots (0.55, 0.70, 0.96)
Download progress of 0 or less (unknown size) switches to a creep toward 0.50 instead of freezing

Verification is threefold on the copied-out app: Developer ID signature for team NARHG44L48 with identifier equal to Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier (fallback literal "iordv.droppycode"), CFBundleShortVersionString equal to the accepted update version, and spctl Gatekeeper acceptance
Signature check flags: kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures | kSecCSCheckNestedCode | kSecCSStrictValidate

Error strings, verbatim: "The downloaded disk image could not be opened. <shell failure>", "The disk image holds no app.", "The update could not be copied. <shell failure>", "The downloaded app is version <actual|unknown>, not <expected>.", "Gatekeeper did not accept the downloaded app. <shell failure>", "The downloaded app is not signed.", "The signature requirement could not be built.", "The downloaded app is not signed by Droppy. <reason|OSStatus n>", "Droppy Code cannot replace itself in <parent path>. Move it to your Applications folder and try again.", "The download had nowhere to go.", "The download failed with HTTP <status>.", "The update could not be downloaded. <error>"
handOff() refuses when the parent of Bundle.main.bundleURL is not writable

Installer script waits for the PID with kill -0 in 0.25 s steps, giving up after i > 240 (about 60 seconds) with the message "The app did not quit"; it also prints "Could not move the installed app aside" and "Could not move the update into place"
Backup path used by the script: "$(dirname "$DEST")/.$(basename "$DEST").previous"; it is restored if the move-in fails and removed on success
The staged app is copied to a path whose last component equals Bundle.main.bundleURL.lastPathComponent, so the installed bundle keeps its filename
The 25 s handoff timeout clears the relaunch marker and calls fail() if the app is somehow still in .handoff (a refused quit)
Downloader is a URLSessionDownloadDelegate so a large image streams to disk; didFinishDownloadingTo moves the temp file immediately and rejects non-2xx responses

Who calls UpdateInstallProgress.armCelebration() and consumeRelaunchMarker() (presumably the About page and AppDelegate) is outside this bundle

files.purpose: The SwiftUI @main entry point: runs the fixed-order launch prologue (notification guard, SIGPIPE ignore, capture prep, legacy migration, hang watchdog, switch latency) and declares a menus-only Settings scene, because the real windows are AppKit windows owned by WindowManager.
side_effects: Installs a framework notification guard before anything posts a notification (DCInstallNotificationGuard)
Sets the SIGPIPE disposition to SIG_IGN process-wide so writes to an exited provider process report EPIPE instead of killing the app
WebsiteCaptures.prepare() runs before any settings or library read
LegacyMigration.run() migrates defaults and the support folder from the former app name
HangWatchdog.start() writes main-thread stacks to ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code when the main thread freezes
SwitchLatency.start()
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI App lifecycle bridged to AppKit with @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor
Settings scene, a macOS-only SwiftUI scene type, used purely as a menu carrier with EmptyView content
POSIX signal(3) with SIGPIPE / SIG_IGN
Log destination ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code (macOS user Logs directory)
Comment cites popover window ordering on macOS 27 as the reason for the notification guard
Real windows are AppKit NSWindows owned by WindowManager, not SwiftUI WindowGroups
ui_elements: Settings { EmptyView() } scene carrying .commands { AppCommands(model: WindowManager.shared.model) } — no SwiftUI-declared app windows at all
feature_notes: Launch order is explicitly load-bearing and commented: DCInstallNotificationGuard() first (before anything posts a notification), then SIGPIPE ignore, then WebsiteCaptures.prepare() and LegacyMigration.run() before anything reads settings or the library, then HangWatchdog.start() and SwitchLatency.start()
A framework observer raising while a notification is posted costs a log line instead of the app, per the guard's comment
The menu bar contents come entirely from AppCommands built over WindowManager.shared.model
unresolved_questions: AppDelegate, DCInstallNotificationGuard, WebsiteCaptures, HangWatchdog, SwitchLatency, WindowManager and AppCommands are all defined outside this bundle, so what each prologue step actually does is not verifiable from this file

files.purpose: One-shot migration from the app's earlier name Cody: copies the old bundle identifier's UserDefaults persistent domain into the current defaults without overwriting existing keys, and renames the Application Support folder Cody to Droppy Code.
state_owned: No instance state; only the three private static string constants and the boolean marker it writes into UserDefaults
side_effects: Reads the persistent domain of another bundle identifier ("iordv.cody") from UserDefaults
Writes every former key whose current value is nil into UserDefaults.standard
Moves ~/Library/Application Support/Cody to ~/Library/Application Support/Droppy Code with try? (failure is silently ignored)
Sets UserDefaults key "migratedFromEarlierName" to true at the end, unconditionally once run reaches that line
platform_assumptions: macOS/Foundation UserDefaults persistent-domain access by bundle identifier
.applicationSupportDirectory in .userDomainMask, taking element [0] of the returned array (~/Library/Application Support)
Directory move semantics of an app support folder as a single filesystem rename
persisted_fields: "migratedFromEarlierName" (UserDefaults.standard, Bool, default false) — the once-only guard; when true, run() returns immediately
Every key found in the persistent domain "iordv.cody" is copied under its own name into UserDefaults.standard, but only where defaults.object(forKey:) is currently nil
feature_notes: run() is skipped entirely when AppInfo.isDevelopment is true, so a development build never migrates
Existing values always win: the loop is `for (key, value) in former where defaults.object(forKey: key) == nil`
The folder move only happens when ~/Library/Application Support/Cody exists AND ~/Library/Application Support/Droppy Code does not, so an existing new-name library is never clobbered
Target folder name literal is "Droppy Code" (with the space), created with isDirectory: true
unresolved_questions: AppInfo.isDevelopment is defined outside this bundle, so what marks a build as development is not verifiable here
The migration marker is written into the current defaults, so whether a former-name key literally called "migratedFromEarlierName" could pre-suppress the migration is unknowable from this file alone

files.purpose: Polls the public GitLab releases API for project 86415974, picks the newest stable non-upcoming release that ships a .dmg asset, persists it, recomputes updateAvailable against the running version, and posts one user notification per newly found version.

feature_notes: AppVersion parses 1 to 3 dot-separated all-digit components, strips a leading v or V, pads with zeros to 3 components, and returns nil for anything with a prerelease suffix such as -nightly. or -beta.1
Comparison is lexicographic over the padded [Int] components
updateAvailable is recomputed from the running version, so an installed update stops reading as available while the notes stay
startBackgroundChecks() is a no-op if already started, if WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, or if AppInfo.isDevelopment; it waits 8 s after launch then checks every 6 hours (21600 s)
Becoming active triggers a catch-up check only when the last check is older than 6 hours, or when there has never been one
check() returns early with updateAvailable when a check is already running, and returns false outright in development builds

newestRelease(in:) skips releases where upcomingRelease is true, where the tag does not parse, where releasedAt is in the future, where no asset link is a disk image, or where the URL will not parse; among the rest it keeps the highest version (ties keep the first, since `if let current = best, current.0 >= version { continue }`)
Link.isDiskImage is true when the lowercased direct_asset_url-or-url path ends in ".dmg" or the lowercased asset name ends in ".dmg"
pageURL is releasesURL.appending(path: release.tagName), i.e. https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases/<tag>

The launch flag `--preview-update 9.9.9` overrides only the reported version of the real newest release, so the update story can be demonstrated; installing it then fails verification unless the real release carries that version
size is filled in by a HEAD request only when the release JSON did not supply one; nothing depends on it
notifyOnce marks the version as notified BEFORE the async add, so a denied or failed add still suppresses future banners for that version

URLSession config: ephemeral, reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData, urlCache nil, request timeout 15 s, resource timeout 30 s, waitsForConnectivity false, headers User-Agent "Droppy Code/<AppInfo.version>" and Accept "application/json"
GitLab JSON field names read: tag_name, name, description, released_at, upcoming_release, assets.links[].name/url/direct_asset_url
Custom decoding is lenient: name, description, released_at optional; upcoming_release defaults to false; assets defaults to Assets(links: [])
parseDate tries ISO8601 with fractional seconds first (example given: 2026-09-13T18:28:42.057Z), then plain internet date time
